title: Blended cost per 1M output tokens (v1) — sample calcs + sensitivity + reconciliation notes
content:
Doc type: Sheet (represented as text)
Last updated: 2025-12-15 (Mei)

Purpose
- Working spreadsheet-style notes for computing “blended $/1M output tokens” (v1) using:
  (a) metered output tokens (hourly, by dims), and
  (b) infra cost inputs (GPU hours * rate card + optional overhead allocations)
- Includes: sample calculations, applying rate card versions, sensitivity analysis (idle allocation, overhead), and reconciliation notes vs Billing.

Audience
- Engineering (Telemetry/Analytics + Observability), Finance/FP&A (methodology), Product (interpretation).

IMPORTANT NOTES / CAVEATS (v1)
- Blended cost is NOT “customer price” and will not match revenue.
- For Dedicated/Private, costs can be capacity-reserved; allocation choices (idle treatment) materially affect $/1M.
- Token metering parity for streaming was a known gap earlier in Q4; for any retro periods pre hotfix, expect undercount risk. See github:redwood/pr-19355.

========================================
TAB: Inputs & definitions
========================================
Definition (v1)
- blended_cost_per_1m_output_tokens = (allocated_cost_usd / output_tokens) * 1,000,000

Where
- output_tokens = sum(metered_output_tokens) for the slice
- allocated_cost_usd (v1) = gpu_compute_cost_usd + (shared_overhead_usd * overhead_allocation_basis)
  - gpu_compute_cost_usd = gpu_hours * gpu_hourly_rate_usd (by region/provider/capacity type)
  - overhead_allocation_basis (default) = proportionate to gpu_compute_cost_usd (finance-friendly) OR gpu_hours (engineering-friendly). Pick one and keep consistent.

Default dimension slice (v1 dashboard)
- by: model (and model_version + quantization_profile), region, customer_tier
- time grain: hourly rollups (displayed daily/weekly in UI)

Inclusion / exclusion (v1 assumptions)
INCLUDE
- GPU compute cost for LLM inference workers (prefill+decode)
- Control-plane / serving overhead that FP&A allocates to “Inference COGS” (if included in rate card or overhead line)
EXCLUDE (v1)
- Non-inference R&D spend
- Sales/marketing costs
- Customer support costs
- One-off incident credits (billing-side)

Token definitions
- output_tokens: tokens generated by model (includes tool-call arguments if emitted as model output; excludes prompt/input tokens)
- streaming parity: output tokens must be counted equivalently for streaming and non-streaming responses

Customer tier mapping (high level)
- self-serve: hosted API default plans
- dedicated: reserved capacity pools (contract flag + routing)
- private: VPC/on-prem private control plane
- enterprise: enterprise plan on hosted (non-dedicated), if applicable in billing metadata

Idle capacity (methodology option)
- Option A (default for “blended”): allocate idle cost to tokens (spreads fixed costs across usage)
- Option B (“marginal” view): exclude idle cost; only allocate utilized GPU time. (Not the exec KPI default.)

Rate card versioning
- Use rate_card_version to pin hourly GPU rates.
- Finance preference: stable per-quarter rate card; changes are versioned (e.g., 2025Q4.v2).

========================================
TAB: Rate card snapshot (2025Q4) — example rows
========================================
Source: gdrive:shared_drives/finance-and-legal/gpu-cost-rate-card-2025q4
Cadence: quarterly baseline; mid-quarter changes are additive versions.

Columns:
- rate_card_version | provider | region_norm | capacity_type | gpu_type | hourly_rate_usd | notes

Example rows (illustrative numbers for testing / sanity checks)
rate_card_version | provider | region_norm | capacity_type | gpu_type | hourly_rate_usd | notes
2025Q4.v1 | aws | us-east-1 | on_demand | h100-sxm | 7.20 | includes infra margin + networking baseline
2025Q4.v1 | aws | us-east-1 | reserved  | h100-sxm | 5.60 | 1y RI equivalent
2025Q4.v1 | aws | us-west-2 | on_demand | h100-sxm | 7.45 | slightly higher regional blended
2025Q4.v1 | gcp | europe-west1 | on_demand | h100-sxm | 7.90 | EU uplift
2025Q4.v1 | gcp | europe-west1 | reserved  | h100-sxm | 6.30 | EU reserved
2025Q4.v1 | aws | eu-west-1 | on_demand | a100-80g | 3.10 | legacy fleet
2025Q4.v1 | aws | us-east-1 | on_demand | a100-80g | 2.85 | legacy fleet

NOTES
- Some pools are mixed GPU types. If pool telemetry only gives gpu_hours without gpu_type, we must infer using pool->gpu_type mapping (risk).

========================================
TAB: Sample calculation (hourly) — compute-only + overhead
========================================
Goal: show end-to-end $/1M output tokens for one hour, then rolled up across multiple slices.

Inputs needed per hour per slice (from aggregation job)
- hour_utc
- region_norm
- customer_tier
- model_id
- model_version
- quantization_profile
- gpu_type
- capacity_type (reserved/on_demand where possible)
- gpu_hours
- output_tokens
- (optional) input_tokens (not used in v1 primary metric)

Example: One hour slice
Assume hour_utc = 2025-12-01T10:00:00Z
rate_card_version = 2025Q4.v1

Row
- region_norm: us-east-1
- customer_tier: self-serve
- model: rw-llama-3.1-70b
- model_version: 3.1-70b.2025-11-15
- quantization_profile: fp16
- gpu_type: h100-sxm
- capacity_type: on_demand
- gpu_hours: 120.0
- output_tokens: 98,500,000
- shared_overhead_pct: 12% (example; see Finance methodology note)

Step-by-step
1) gpu_compute_cost_usd = gpu_hours * hourly_rate
   = 120.0 * 7.20 = 864.00
2) overhead_usd = gpu_compute_cost_usd * shared_overhead_pct
   = 864.00 * 0.12 = 103.68
3) allocated_cost_usd = 864.00 + 103.68 = 967.68
4) blended_cost_per_1m_output_tokens = (allocated_cost_usd / output_tokens) * 1,000,000
   = (967.68 / 98,500,000) * 1,000,000
   = 9.83 USD / 1M output tokens

Sanity check
- Order of magnitude: $10 / 1M output tokens for a large model on H100 with decent throughput is plausible.

Example: Roll-up across 3 slices (same hour)
Columns
slice | gpu_hours | rate | gpu_cost | overhead% | overhead | allocated_cost | output_tokens | $/1M
A (70B fp16) | 120.0 | 7.20 | 864.00 | 12% | 103.68 | 967.68 | 98,500,000 | 9.83
B (70B int8) | 90.0  | 7.20 | 648.00 | 12% | 77.76  | 725.76 | 92,000,000 | 7.89
C (8B int8)  | 25.0  | 2.85 | 71.25  | 12% | 8.55   | 79.80  | 160,000,000 | 0.50

Roll-up formula (IMPORTANT)
- For rollups, DO NOT average the $/1M values.
- Correct rollup = (sum allocated_cost) / (sum output_tokens) * 1,000,000

Roll-up calc
- sum allocated_cost = 967.68 + 725.76 + 79.80 = 1,773.24
- sum output_tokens = 98.5M + 92.0M + 160.0M = 350.5M
- blended $/1M = (1,773.24 / 350,500,000) * 1,000,000 = 5.06

========================================
TAB: Idle allocation sensitivity (Dedicated focus)
========================================
Why this matters
- Dedicated pools: customer may reserve N GPUs; actual utilization varies hour-to-hour.
- Finance (blended) tends to allocate the full reserved cost across tokens during the window (Option A), which makes $/1M spike when usage drops.

Scenario
- Customer tier: dedicated
- Region: europe-west1
- GPU type: h100-sxm (reserved)
- rate (reserved): $6.30/hr
- Reserved capacity for this customer: 64 GPUs
- Hour window: 1 hour
- Effective reserved gpu_hours = 64 * 1 = 64 gpu_hours
- Utilized gpu_hours (from telemetry) = 38 gpu_hours
- Output tokens generated = 22,000,000
- overhead_pct = 10% (example)

Option A: Allocate FULL reserved cost (blended, includes idle)
- gpu_cost = reserved_gpu_hours * rate = 64 * 6.30 = 403.20
- overhead = 40.32
- allocated_cost = 443.52
- $/1M = (443.52 / 22,000,000)*1,000,000 = 20.16

Option B: Allocate UTILIZED cost only (marginal, excludes idle)
- gpu_cost = utilized_gpu_hours * rate = 38 * 6.30 = 239.40
- overhead = 23.94
- allocated_cost = 263.34
- $/1M = (263.34 / 22,000,000)*1,000,000 = 11.97

Idle delta
- Absolute delta: 8.19 $/1M
- Interpretation: This is a “utilization effect” not a runtime regression.

Recommended dashboard behavior (v1)
- Primary metric: Option A (Finance-aligned blended)
- Secondary toggle (not required v1 UI): “exclude idle” for engineering investigations
- If we ship only Option A, we should add a visible annotation when dedicated utilization drops (e.g., reserved vs utilized ratio).

========================================
TAB: Overhead sensitivity (global)
========================================
Overhead can be applied as:
- % of GPU compute cost (default)
- $ per GPU hour (if FP&A provides a normalized value)
- separate line items (network egress, storage, control plane) allocated by different drivers

Simple sensitivity for one rollup
Base (from sample calc): gpu_compute_cost = 1,583.25; output_tokens = 350,500,000

Assume overhead_pct in {0%, 8%, 12%, 18%}

overhead% | allocated_cost | blended $/1M
0%  | 1,583.25 | 4.52
8%  | 1,709.91 | 4.88
12% | 1,773.24 | 5.06
18% | 1,868.24 | 5.33

Takeaway
- Overhead assumption moves KPI ~+18% from 0%->18% in this example.
- We need to pin overhead model + version and treat changes as methodology revisions.

========================================
TAB: Reconciliation notes vs Billing (what matches / what doesn’t)
========================================
What Finance wants
- Dashboard blended cost should reconcile to infra spend inputs (COGS) within an agreed tolerance after allocations.

What Support/Product sometimes expects (but should NOT)
- Dashboard cost should match customer invoice totals. (Incorrect; invoices include margin, discounts, credits, plan min-commit, etc.)

Reconciliation surfaces
A) Cost-to-spend reconciliation (preferred)
- Compare sum(allocated_cost_usd) vs. sum(source_infra_cost_usd) for the same time window and scope.
- Must ensure same:
  - timezone cut (UTC vs local)
  - included regions
  - inclusion of idle
  - reserved amortization window
  - rate_card_version

B) Tokens-to-metering reconciliation
- Compare sum(output_tokens) in unit economics tables vs metering raw fact tables.
- Common drift causes:
  - streaming path undercount (historical)
  - dropped rows due to null region mapping
  - high-cardinality tag guardrails rejecting events

C) Cost-to-billing reconciliation (informational only)
- Expect differences; track them with explanation buckets.

Known difference buckets (billing vs blended cost)
- Revenue includes margin; cost does not.
- Customer discounts/commits/credits not modeled in cost.
- Billing token definitions sometimes differ (e.g., billed tokens include input+output; our KPI is output-only).
- Rounding + aggregation grain differences.
- Dedicated invoices may be flat monthly regardless of hourly usage.

Checklist: When someone says “dashboard doesn’t match billing”
1) Confirm they’re comparing “cost” vs “price”.
2) Confirm token basis: output-only vs total tokens.
3) Confirm time window boundaries and timezone.
4) Check rate card version used.
5) For dedicated: check idle inclusion.
6) Run raw metering parity query for streaming vs non-streaming mix.

Suggested reconciliation tolerance bands (draft)
- Spend reconciliation (hosted, aggregated daily): within ±2–3% once pipeline stable
- Spend reconciliation (dedicated/private, monthly): within ±3–6% depending on idle + amortization assumptions

========================================
TAB: Notes / open questions (WIP)
========================================
Open questions (need sign-off)
- Overhead allocation: % of GPU cost vs per-gpu-hour vs multi-driver model? (Finance preference seems % of GPU cost for v1.)
- Dedicated idle allocation: confirm default is “include idle” for exec KPI.
- Mixed GPU pools: do we have reliable pool->gpu_type mapping for all regions?
- Region normalization: confirm that “unknown” rows are kept (not dropped) and appear in dashboard as “Unknown/Unmapped” with warning.

Implementation notes (for ENG-8426/PM-483)
- Ensure we store:
  - rate_card_version
  - methodology_version (for overhead/idle policy)
  - allocation_basis flags
- Materialized view should include rollup-friendly columns (allocated_cost_usd numerator and output_tokens denominator), not only $/1M.

Notes to self (Mei)
- Make sure the warehouse view exposes reserved_gpu_hours and utilized_gpu_hours for dedicated slices (even if v1 UI hides it).
- Add a minimal unit test dataset where rollup correctness is validated (no averaging of ratios).
- Ask Caleb if we can include a “coverage/confidence” indicator derived from % rows with non-null region_norm + customer_tier + model_id.
